brief.topic: The Quiet Rhythm of Moving Inward

s01: Two small weights circle on a turning platform.
Bringing them inward can make the turn quicker.
Look down at the same platform.
We will ignore outside twisting forces and friction.
The moving weights are part of the system, along with the platform.
A mass farther from the center contributes more rotational inertia.
For a small weight, that contribution grows with the square of its distance.
Move it halfway inward, and its contribution becomes one quarter.
The total rotational inertia falls, so the angular speed rises.
Their product, angular momentum, stays the same in this model.
The platform itself still has inertia, so the speed does not simply become four times as large.
The extra energy comes from the work of pulling inward.
Conserving angular momentum does not mean conserving rotational energy.
Let the weights move outward again and watch the turn ease.
Distance from the center is a quiet way to change the rhythm of a rotating system.

scenes.narration:
Two small weights circle on a turning platform. Bringing them inward can make the turn quicker.

Look down at the same platform. We will ignore outside twisting forces and friction. The moving weights are part of the system, along with the platform.

A mass farther from the center contributes more rotational inertia. For a small weight, that contribution grows with the square of its distance. Move it halfway inward, and its contribution becomes one quarter.

Draw both weights inward now. The total rotational inertia falls, so the angular speed rises. Their product, angular momentum, stays the same in this model. The platform itself still has inertia, so the speed does not simply become four times as large.

The extra energy comes from the work of pulling inward. Conserving angular momentum does not mean conserving rotational energy. Let the weights move outward again and watch the turn ease. Distance from the center is a quiet way to change the rhythm of a rotating system.
